answer: In an agent economy, each participant must deposit a stake into a shared escrow at the digital wharf before receiving work. Peer validators then pass the agents action history through an umber-tinted prism that splits behavioral signals into distinct bands; only those whose patterns match long-term consistent identities across multiple bands receive attestation. Creating sybil identities forces an attacker to lock separate stakes for every fake, each of which can be slashed if any single band fails the prism check, rapidly multiplying capital requirements.
